newsitem.title: USA: GM N. American output to fall in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: GM N. American output to fall in fourth quarter.

text.p: General Motors Corp., facing several critical new product launches this fall, said it expects its fourth quarter North American production to fall 3.8 percent from a year earlier.

GM said it has scheduled production of 1.32 million cars and trucks in the United States, Canada and Mexico during the October-December preiod, compared to 1.372 million vehicles it built in the same period of 1995.
GM also said it increased its third quarter production forecast by 5,000 units from estimates made a month ago.

The world's largest automaker now plans to build 1.245 million cars and trucks in North America the during the third quarter, a 5.7 percent increase over the 1.178 million vehicles it built a year earlier.
For the full 1996 calendar year, GM said its North American production forecast now stands at 5.332 million units, down 5.5 percent from the 5.645 million vehicles it built in 1995.
In the fourth quarter, GM's production will be partially curtailed by launches of new vehicles, including several new sedans and a trio of new minivans.
In the first quarter of 1996, GM's production was curtailed by a 17-day strike at two Dayton, Ohio, brake plants that forced the automaker to idle nearly all of its North American assembly plants.
During the month of August, GM said it produced a total of 484,000 vehicles in the United States, Canada and Mexico, including 287,000 passenger cars and 197,000 trucks.
